commits.title: A page's motion needs say whether it needs the sheet at all

changes.how: Only on the 'built' path. The type MotionNeeds has the flags js, view and any (see motionNeeds() around line 279). `any` is set by motionOf() for entrance, hover and scroll effects only. Add a fourth flag `css: boolean` that is true when ANYTHING motion.css styles is on the page. Set it in motionNeeds(): whenever `any` is set; whenever a row, column, inner column has backgroundMotion, backgroundLayers (non-empty) or a gradient background; and for every other source of a data-fx-* attribute. To find every source, list the attributes the sheet styles: rg -o '\[data-fx-[a-z-]+' src/app/motion.css | sort -u (33 names today, among them amb, bglayer, bgm, bgroot, blob, clip, disc, each, enter, fade, flow, g, glow, grad, gradient, grain, hover, in, layer, layers, live, nofade, pattern, pic, ready, scroll, soft, split, sr, text, tl, trigger, w), and for each find where it is written: rg -n 'data-fx-<name>|"fx-<name>"|fx<Name>' src -g '!*.test.*' -g '!*.css'. Today the writers are in src/lib/motion-attrs.ts, src/lib/background-layers.ts, src/lib/motion-runtime.ts, src/components/page-parts.tsx, src/components/page-article.tsx, src/components/background-video.tsx and src/components/motion-runtime.tsx. Each writer's condition (the block, row or column setting that makes it write the attribute) must set `css` in motionNeeds(). Attributes only the runtime script sets after load (ready, in, live) need no source of their own: they only appear where another attribute already did.

Add the gate test: read src/app/motion.css, collect every distinct data-fx-* attribute name in its selectors, and for each name assert it is a key of a table in the test, `SOURCES`, that maps the attribute to a small page (one row, built with the test helpers other motion tests use) on which motionNeeds(rows).css must be true. A new selector with an attribute that has no SOURCES entry fails the test with: 'motion.css styles [data-fx-NAME]; add the page setting that writes it to SOURCES and make motionNeeds() set css for it'. Runtime-only attributes (ready, in, live) are listed in a second constant with the reason.

commits.title: motion.css is linked by the pages that need it and leaves the site's sheet

changes.how: A prebuild script, plain Node with built-ins only (node:fs, node:path, node:crypto), run from anywhere (root = path.join(import.meta.dirname, '..')). It reads src/app/motion.css and writes, unchanged and unminified, the line `@layer theme, base, components, utilities;` followed by the file's whole text: motion.css already puts its rules inside its own `@layer components { … }` (line 24 to the end) with one `@property` above it, and uses no Tailwind directive, so it needs no compile and no wrapping (lightningcss is not a direct dependency of the repo and pnpm does not hoist it: do not import it). It computes the first 8 hex characters of the written content's sha256, writes public/motion.<hash>.css, deletes any other public/motion.*.css, and writes src/lib/motion-sheet.generated.ts with `// Written by scripts/motion-sheet.mjs: do not edit.` and `export const MOTION_SHEET = "/motion.<hash>.css";`. Add `/public/motion.*.css` and `/src/lib/motion-sheet.generated.ts` to .gitignore. Run it in three places so the generated module exists wherever code is checked or built: (1) package.json `"postinstall": "node scripts/motion-sheet.mjs"` (pnpm runs the root project's own postinstall on every `pnpm install`, which every CI job and Vercel's build do before lint, typecheck, the tests or the build; pnpm 10 blocks only dependencies' scripts); (2) `"predev": "node scripts/motion-sheet.mjs"`, so an edit of motion.css shows in dev; (3) scripts/next-build.mjs, before next starts: `execFileSync(process.execPath, [path.join(import.meta.dirname, 'motion-sheet.mjs')], { stdio: 'inherit' })` (import execFileSync from node:child_process and path from node:path if the file lacks them), so a build always ships the current hash. Add no pretest, pretypecheck or prelint script: postinstall already covers CI's static, int and gate jobs. It needs no service and no paid plan.

Import MOTION_SHEET from "@/lib/motion-sheet.generated". When `needs.css` is true, draw `<link rel="stylesheet" href={MOTION_SHEET} precedence="motion" />` before the existing noscript and runtime parts (React hoists a stylesheet link with a precedence into the head and holds the paint for it; see the CSS guide in read_first for why an imported sheet cannot do this). Keep the noscript style and <MotionRuntime /> exactly as they are. MotionSupport is drawn by src/components/page-article.tsx (the page's rows) and src/components/site-parts.tsx (header and footer rows), so a page links the sheet when its page, header or footer needs it, and Kaizena Flow's own pages go through the same two parts.

After step 2.11 there are two Tailwind entries. In the SITE's entry remove the line `@import "./motion.css";` (it is line 10 of src/app/globals.css today; if step 2.11 moved the site's entry to another file, remove it there: rg -n 'motion.css' src/app -g '*.css'). In the ADMIN's entry keep the import: the builder's canvas draws motion without MotionSupport. If only one entry exists (2.11 not done), stop.

The case 'is imported by the global stylesheet, after Tailwind' (line 18) changes to two expectations: the site's entry does NOT import ./motion.css, and the admin's entry does, after its Tailwind import. Add: MOTION_SHEET matches /^\/motion\.[0-9a-f]{8}\.css$/.

Lower the site's stylesheet budget that step 2.11 set to the figures the build now gives (at most 116,500 raw and 17,400 Brotli). Add two expectations: the demo store's home (no builder motion) has no <link> whose href matches /motion\.[0-9a-f]{8}\.css/; a page with one entrance effect (use the page e2e/motion.spec.ts already opens) has exactly one.

do_not: Do not build anything if step 1.23's share is 50% or more, or if the reading is missing. The decision is the reading's, not yours.
Do not delete or shrink any rule of motion.css: nothing in it is dead.
Do not remove the motion import from the admin's entry: the builder's canvas needs it.
Do not import motion.css from a layout or a component (Next keeps an imported global sheet on every later page of the session and bundles it with the segment); the link is hand-made.
Do not make MotionRuntime or the noscript style depend on the new css flag; they keep their own flags.
Do not commit public/motion.*.css or the generated module.
stop_if: docs/performance.md has no reading of the share from step 1.23.
The share is between 40% and 60%: report it; a change of this size on a coin toss is the owner's call.
